question.problem:
Given the function $f(x,y,z)={x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}$, compute ${∇}_{x,z}({∇}_{x,z}\,f).$
${∇}_{x,z}({∇}_{x,z}f)=\text{ }$ {{field-1}} {{field-2}}
{{field-3}} {{field-4}}
question.worked_solution:
First, we take the variable subset gradient:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∇}_{x,z}\,f & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}) \\ \frac{∂}{∂z}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2})\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2x \\ 2z\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the second derivatives with respect to $x$ and $z$:

$$
\begin{aligned} & \frac{∂}{∂x}(2x)=2\,\, &  & \frac{∂}{∂z}(2x)=0 \\  & \frac{∂}{∂x}(2z)=0\,\, &  & \frac{∂}{∂z}(2z)=2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∇}_{x,z}({∇}_{x,z}\,f) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂z} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂z∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{z}^{2}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
